assessment:
Three wishes, and they do not overlap. Know which one you are holding before you decide what is missing.

Reach first. Enlightened Tutor takes an artifact or an enchantment — 15 of them in the 99. Worldly Tutor takes any creature card, which is 29 in the library, since the commander is in the command zone and no search reaches it. Sarkhan's Triumph takes a Dragon creature card and nothing else: 21 in the library, and no reducer at all. The four cost reducers besides the commander are Urza's Incubator, Herald's Horn, Dragonspeaker Shaman and Dragonlord's Servant — two artifacts and two non-Dragon bodies, a Human Barbarian Shaman and a Goblin Shaman. Enlightened Tutor reaches the two artifacts, Worldly Tutor reaches the two bodies, Sarkhan's Triumph reaches none. You draw a reducer by turn six in 42.2% of games without a tutor and 59.9% with tutors modelled, mean turn 3.264 (◆ goldfish, 10,000 seeded iterations). That 17.7-point gap is what these three cards are worth on the deck's own curve fixer, measured rather than asserted.

Delivery second. Sarkhan's Triumph puts the card in your hand. The other two shuffle and put it on top, so they cost you a draw step: cast them at the end of the turn before yours and collect the card on your own draw. Cast one on your own turn and you have paid a full rotation for nothing.

One card shortens that wait and only for Dragons. Herald's Horn, with Dragon chosen, hands you a topped Dragon creature card on your upkeep. Nothing in this list casts spells off the top — the effect that used to do that is not in the 99 any more — so for Enlightened Tutor the wait is always real. Read the 15 artifacts and enchantments and none of them carries Creature in its type line, so the Horn's upkeep look can never return one.

Colour third. Worldly Tutor asks {G}, at 84.9% on curve from lands alone and 91.8% with rocks and dorks. Enlightened Tutor asks {W} at 78.7% and 86.6%. Sarkhan's Triumph asks {2}{R} at 71.8% and 82.2% (◆ mana-analysis). The two one-mana tutors are also the ones you can hold up on a turn you are already doing something.

What is proven, and what is only declared. Four checker-passed stacks describe boards this list can still make: 001, 002, 005 and 007. Stacks 003, 004 and 006 name Aggravated Assault, Savage Ventmaw, Blasphemous Act and Wrathful Red Dragon, none of which is in the 99, and all three are marked not presentable — the verdicts stand, the boards cannot be built. There is no infinite left here. The deck declares two kills and its own targets file labels both UNVERIFIED in their titles: the entry kill assembles by turn six in 15.0% of games and 31.6% with tutors modelled, the combat kill in 15.7% and 34.5% (◆ goldfish). Point a wish at either. Do not tell yourself you are fetching an infinite.

Last, the funding rule, which is narrower than it looks. Six sources in the 99 make restricted mana (◆ deck-facts): Cavern of Souls, Delighted Halfling, Desolation of Smaug, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, Sarkhan, Fireblood and Unclaimed Territory. Read every one and not a single coloured pip on a tutor is payable from them. Cavern of Souls and Unclaimed Territory make creature-spell-of-the-chosen-type mana; Desolation of Smaug and Sarkhan, Fireblood make Dragon-spells-only mana; Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon makes Dragon-or-Omen mana; the Halfling's any-colour mode is legendary-spells-only. Four of them — Cavern, Unclaimed Territory, Maelstrom and the Halfling — also carry a plain '{T}: Add {C}', and that colourless mana pays the {2} of Sarkhan's Triumph and nothing else on this sheet. None of it pays Sneak Attack's {R} either: colourless cannot pay a coloured cost, and the restricted modes are for spells while the activation is an ability. Count unrestricted red before you plan the turn.

targets.scenario: Turn two or three, at the end of the turn before yours. Two or three lands down, and nothing in your hand costs less than four.
targets.why: Buy the discount before you buy anything else. You draw one of the four cost reducers by turn six in 42.2% of games, mean turn 3.264 when you get one (◆ goldfish) — so in more than half of your games you do not have one, and this is the wish that fixes the hand you were actually dealt. Incubator takes {2} off every Dragon creature spell and stacks with eminence's {1}, so your six-drops cost three and The Ur-Dragon drops from nine to seven — eminence reads 'other Dragon spells' and does not cut his own cost, Incubator does. Take Herald's Horn instead when your hand is empty rather than heavy: {1} less, and its upkeep look feeds you Dragons you have not drawn yet. ★

targets.scenario: Mid-game, four or five lands on the battlefield and the wrong ones. The commander is castable on mana count and not on colours, or Miirym is stuck behind two of her three.
targets.why: Fetch the fixing, not the payoff. The commander alone asks for all five colours at {4}{W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, and black is the thinnest of them at 44.1% on curve from lands alone and 63.6% once rocks and dorks are counted, against 71.8% red, 78.7% white, 81.0% blue and 84.9% green (◆ mana-analysis). Only two cards in the 99 want black at all — The Ur-Dragon and Crux of Fate — so this is a commander problem rather than a spell problem. Twelve of the 32 land entries enter tapped. Lantern gives every land you already control 'add one mana of any color', so it repairs the board in front of you instead of the board you might draw. ★

targets.scenario: A per-Dragon payoff is already down — Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks or Scourge of Valkas — and your hand holds a Dragon you cannot pay for.
targets.why: Stop paying for Dragons and start renting them. Stack 005 priced it exactly: {R} puts Drakuseth, Maw of Flames onto the battlefield with haste, the attack trigger deals 4 and 3 and 3 before blockers, it connects for 7 in the air, and all 17 damage stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice (✓ rules-verified). The same stack settles what it cannot do: Sneak Attack takes a creature card from your HAND, so the commander in the command zone never moves. It is an enchantment, so land it before the sweeper rather than after. One warning that comes from your mana rather than the card: the {R} is an activated ability, and none of the six restricted sources can pay it.

targets.scenario: Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm has survived a rotation, Terror of the Peaks and Dragon Tempest are down, and you still hold a nontoken Dragon.
targets.why: Two stacks bracket this one, and together they say the doubler is the kill rather than the margin. Stack 002 resolved that exact board with Panharmonicon: one Lathliss cast made two nonlegendary copies and 64 damage in 12 separately targeted instances, killing a 32-life opponent outright (✓ rules-verified). Stack 007 resolved the same cast with Panharmonicon removed and nothing else changed: one copy, 20 damage in 4 instances, and the 32-life seat survives at 12 — a 68.75% loss, because the doubler was doubling Terror and both Dragon Tempest abilities on every entry as well as Miirym (✓ rules-verified). Cast the artifact on a quiet turn and hold the Dragon for the loud one. Two things to know before you count on a bigger number: the copies are tokens and the 'nontoken' clause on Miirym and on Lathliss skips them, which is what keeps the cascade finite; and every one of 002's twelve instances reads 'any target', so aimed at a single seat the running total passes 40 by the eighth and a 40-life player is killable from that board.

tutors.notes: One white mana at instant speed, and the card goes on TOP — cast it at the end of the turn before yours so your own draw step collects it. Nothing in this deck shortcuts that wait for an artifact or an enchantment: Herald's Horn looks only for a Dragon creature card, and none of the 15 artifacts and enchantments in the 99 is a creature. The search is revealed, so treat casting it as an announcement. Reveal Sneak Attack two turns before you use it and you have told the table which permanent to kill — game 003 is the record of what that costs, a loss in which the pilot's own reading was that he broadcast the win a turn before he could present it. If that table is in front of you again, the same {W} buys Lightning Greaves instead: haste and shroud, and you hold protection by turn six in only 56.5% of games without a tutor (◆ goldfish). ★

targets.scenario: Turn six or later, at an opponent's end step. You will have five mana next turn, the commander is still in the command zone, and the table has stopped watching your combat step.
targets.why: Rent the commander instead of buying him. The Ur-Dragon has a mean cast turn of 6.916 and a median of 7; he arrives by turn six in 32.9% of games, and in 2,222 of 10,000 he never arrives by turn ten at all (◆ goldfish). Courser costs {4}{R}{R}, five with eminence, and his entry puts The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield with haste — so you attack, draw a card for each attacking Dragon, and put a permanent from hand onto the battlefield, and he returns to the command zone at end step with no tax accrued. Fetch at their end step, cast on yours, attack the same turn.

targets.scenario: Dragon Tempest is on the battlefield, you can reach seven mana next turn including {W}{W}, and one opponent has no flying blocker.
targets.why: This is the deck's loudest contained line and it has a stack behind it. Ancient Gold Dragon costs {5}{W}{W}, six with eminence; connect once and the d20 makes that many 1/1 flying Faerie Dragons at the same time. Stack 001 fixed the roll at 15 and resolved the cascade: Dragon Tempest triggers fifteen times, each trigger dealt X = 17 on that board of two other Dragons, and the 30-life opponent died to the second trigger aimed at them (✓ rules-verified). Two findings from that stack to plan around. Miirym does not copy the tokens, because they are tokens. And every trigger locks its target when it goes on the stack, so triggers aimed at a player who has already left the game fizzle — spread them rather than stacking them on one seat. Two costs before you fetch: {W}{W} on a deck at 78.7% white on curve from lands alone (◆ mana-analysis), and no goldfish figure prices this card at all, since meta.combat_effects_not_modelled names Ancient Gold Dragon as the one combat effect the model cannot read.

targets.scenario: Turn five or six, you missed a land drop, and the top of your hand is stranded behind your mana.
targets.why: Fetch mana wearing a Dragon. Goldspan Dragon costs {3}{R}{R}, four with eminence, and has haste — so it attacks the turn it lands, makes a Treasure, and that Treasure taps for TWO mana of one colour rather than one. It makes another whenever it becomes the target of a spell, yours included. Your land drop hit rate is 65.0% on turn five and 54.4% on turn six (◆ goldfish), so the turn you miss one is a turn to expect rather than to be surprised by. Take Smaug the Magnificent instead when you need the body a turn earlier: {2}{R}{R}, three with eminence, haste, and a Treasure every upkeep whether or not you attack. You draw one of the six Treasure sources by turn six in 56.0% of games and 70.0% with tutors modelled (◆ goldfish) — treat both as floors, because meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled names Atsushi, the Blazing Sky, Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge and Ganax, Astral Hunter as unreadable to the model.

targets.scenario: Two or three Dragons already attacking, and no way to make the swing lethal this turn.
targets.why: Take the multiplier rather than another body. Thrakkus costs {3}{R}{G}, four with eminence, and doubles the power of each Dragon you control when he attacks — a pair of 5/5 Dragon tokens swings as 10/5s. This is one half of what the targets file calls THE COMBAT KILL, and that file labels it UNVERIFIED in its own title: it assembles by turn six in 15.7% of games without a tutor and 34.5% with tutors modelled, and by turn ten in 24.3% and 50.1% (◆ goldfish). No stack has resolved it, so play it as a clock, not as a kill. Atarka, World Render is the same wish two mana up if double strike suits the board better; Thrakkus is the one you can fetch and cast on the same turn off seven mana.

tutors.notes: The only tutor here that puts the card in your HAND — no transit turn, no draw step spent — so this is the one you cast on the turn you need the card, and the one to keep for the piece you cannot afford to telegraph a turn early. It pays for that with reach: 21 Dragon creature cards in the library and nothing else. No Sneak Attack, no Panharmonicon, no land, and none of the four cost reducers, since Urza's Incubator and Herald's Horn are artifacts while Dragonspeaker Shaman is a Human and Dragonlord's Servant a Goblin. It is also the most expensive of the three at {2}{R}, on the colour that runs 71.8% on curve from lands alone and 82.2% with rocks and dorks (◆ mana-analysis). Three mana at instant speed still means you shop on somebody else's end step and keep your whole turn to cast what you found.

targets.scenario: Turn one or two with a green source open. Your keep was two lands and a fistful of five-drops, with no reducer and no rock.
targets.why: Fetch the discount in the one place Enlightened Tutor cannot reach it. Dragonspeaker Shaman costs {1}{R}{R} and takes {2} off every Dragon spell — the same discount as Urza's Incubator, one mana cheaper and a turn earlier, and it needs no type chosen on entry. You hold a reducer by turn six in 42.2% of games and a reducer plus ramp in only 33.6% (◆ goldfish), and that second number is the hand that casts a Dragon on curve. Take Dragonlord's Servant instead when you will only have two mana next turn: {1}{R}, {1} off, on the board a turn sooner. Neither is a Dragon, so Herald's Horn will not shortcut the top of your library here and the transit turn is real.

targets.scenario: Turn one with a green source, holding the commander or Miirym and lands that make two colours between them.
targets.why: Fetch the colour, not the acceleration. Birds of Paradise is the only creature in the 99 that mana-analysis counts as a source for all five colours — Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder and Delighted Halfling produce nothing in that count, because the first two are conditional on the colours you already control and the Halfling's any-colour mana is legendary-spells-only. Ignoble Hierarch covers three. Black runs 44.1% on curve from lands alone and 63.6% with rocks and dorks, and the commander needs it alongside four others (◆ mana-analysis). One mana on turn one is also the only ramp that beats the reducer to the board. Two assumptions to hold: the mana-analysis count gives a creature no survival discount, and game 003 is the record of a pod that removed everything — if that table is in front of you, Chromatic Lantern off the other tutor does the same job and does not die to a fight spell. ★

targets.scenario: Mid-game with five mana and three colours available. Terror of the Peaks or Dragon Tempest is already down and your hand still holds nontoken Dragons.
targets.why: Fetch the doubler before you fetch a body, because everything after her arrives twice. Every nontoken Dragon you cast brings a token copy, and stack 002 resolved what that is worth beside Panharmonicon: one Lathliss cast, two Lathliss copies, 64 damage in twelve targeted instances (✓ rules-verified). Stack 007 is the same board without the artifact and is worth reading in the same breath — one copy, 20 damage, no kill (✓ rules-verified) — so she is a payoff engine rather than a kill by herself. She costs {3}{G}{U}{R}, five with eminence, which is three colours on a deck where green is 84.9% on curve from lands alone, blue 81.0% and red 71.8% (◆ mana-analysis) — check the second and third colour before you fetch, not after. Ward {2} is why she survives the rotation you need her to survive.

targets.scenario: Sneak Attack is on the battlefield, you have {R} plus one green, and you need damage this turn rather than a board next turn.
targets.why: One green mana turns a dead draw step into stack 005's line: Drakuseth on top, {R} to put him in with haste, 4 and 3 and 3 from the attack trigger before blockers, 7 more in the air, and all 17 damage standing after the end-step sacrifice (✓ rules-verified). Pick the three targets before you activate rather than after — the trigger locks them when it goes on the stack. Hard cast he is {4}{R}{R}{R}, six with eminence, against mean available mana of 6.734 on turn six (◆ goldfish), so paying for him is a fair turn-six plan and Sneak Attack is what makes him a turn-four one for {R}.

tutors.notes: One green mana — tied with Enlightened Tutor for the cheapest of the three — and the widest inside its type: any creature card, 29 of them in the library, which is the only route to the two cost reducers that are not artifacts and the only route to a mana dork. {G} is the most reliable of the five colours at 84.9% on curve from lands alone and 91.8% with rocks and dorks (◆ mana-analysis), so this is the tutor you can hold up on a turn you are also casting something. It puts the card on top, so cast it at the end of the turn before yours. Herald's Horn's upkeep trigger pulls a topped Dragon creature card into your hand for nothing, which shortens the wait for Miirym or Drakuseth — it does nothing for Dragonspeaker Shaman, Birds of Paradise or any other non-Dragon.

gaps: There is no infinite left to fetch. Aggravated Assault and Savage Ventmaw left the 99, and so did Blasphemous Act and Wrathful Red Dragon: stacks 003 and 006 name the first pair, stack 004 the second, and all three are marked not presentable — the verdicts stand, the boards cannot be built. Stacks 001, 002, 005 and 007 are what remain. deck-facts finds one combo line fully contained in this deck and zero two-card infinites. If you catch yourself spending a wish 'on the combo', you are working from an old sheet.

Both of the deck's declared kills are unverified, and this guide points wishes at them anyway. THE ENTRY KILL assembles by turn six in 15.0% of games and THE COMBAT KILL in 15.7% (31.6% and 34.5% with tutors modelled, ◆ goldfish); goldfish_targets.json labels both UNVERIFIED in their own titles because no stack has resolved either. A resolve-stack run on Thrakkus or Atarka doubling an attacking Dragon board, or on Utvara Hellkite making a token per attacker underneath a per-Dragon payoff, would settle the combat half.

No wish reaches the graveyard, and this is now absolute rather than nearly so: a search of every oracle text in the 99 for 'from your graveyard' returns zero cards. Nothing here rebuys a Dragon that has died and nothing recovers one that has been exiled. Play around removal rather than planning to answer it — game 003 is a loss to exactly that, a board built and then taken apart by three seats at once.

Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon is a fourth search this guide does not cover: {4}, {T}, sacrifice it, find a Dragon card and put it into your hand. It is a land, so it belongs to the mana analysis rather than to this sheet — but price it before you rely on it, because it costs four mana plus the land itself, and unlike Fabled Passage and Prismatic Vista it puts no land back. It is the one search here that costs you a permanent outright.

No wish here answers a mana-denial permanent, and that is a choice rather than an oversight. After game 001 the pilot declined to build around Blood Moon and named it an accepted risk at bracket 3+. Note also that game 001's verdict — mana consistency is the bottleneck — was recorded against a 31-land list. The base is 36 lands now and game 003, the only logged game on the current decklist sha, reads 'the mana worked'. The Chromatic Lantern and Birds of Paradise wishes above are sized against the deck's colour arithmetic, not against that older reading.

The Treasure and combat figures quoted here are floors, and the model names its own blind spots: meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled lists Atsushi, the Blazing Sky, Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge and Ganax, Astral Hunter, and meta.combat_effects_not_modelled lists Ancient Gold Dragon. One disagreement to hand to the orchestrator rather than to resolve here: the authored label on that goldfish target says the model can SPEND only two of the six Treasure sources, while the meta block names three it cannot read, which leaves three. The label is authored and the meta block is computed; the guide quotes the meta block.

engine.json is stale against this decklist and is therefore not used as a source of composition anywhere above. Seventeen cards it assigns to stages are not in the 99, including Rapacious Dragon, Korlessa, Scale Singer, Moltensteel Dragon and Smothering Tithe — the same rot that this guide was rewritten to clear. Its stage labels are still the deck's vocabulary; its card lists need a re-run of analyze-engine.
